title: Apply the canon hierarchy
requirement: Every program decision MUST preserve Book I, implement Book II, follow Book III, respect Book IV ownership, and use Book X semantics; conflict MUST halt the affected decision and be recorded.

title: Separate protection from restraint
requirement: Every risk assessment and control design MUST state whether it protects HAL, prevents HAL from exceeding Authority, or does both; neither objective MAY be omitted when applicable.

title: Assign control accountability
requirement: Each active control MUST have one accountable Control Owner, identified operators, an assessor, evidence, test frequency, failure response, and succession coverage.

title: Classify risk by consequence
requirement: Risks MUST be classified using the highest material consequence across authority, constitutional invariant, privacy, trust boundary, compromise, continuity, safety, irreversibility, and blast radius.

title: Maintain separation of duties
requirement: No person or service MAY solely request, approve, execute, and attest a protected security, privacy, trust, key, Treaty, or break-glass change.

title: Operate a control lifecycle
requirement: Controls MUST be proposed, reviewed, approved, implemented, tested, monitored, remediated, and retired through versioned records with preserved history.

title: Time-bound all exceptions
requirement: An exception MUST identify control, scope, rationale, risk, compensating controls, approver, evidence, effective date, review date, expiry, and revocation triggers; silent or permanent exceptions are prohibited.

title: Forbid program-created authority
requirement: Security status, trust, identity, credentials, certificates, risk acceptance, or control compliance MUST NOT create Permission, Authority, Owner approval, capability-class approval, or Treaty scope.

title: Bind access to immutable identity
requirement: Every access decision MUST bind an authenticated immutable principal identity; names, locations, devices, network zones, or roles alone MUST NOT establish identity.

title: Independently evaluate Permission for every action
requirement: Successful authentication MUST NOT imply Permission; each protected operation MUST obtain a current Permission decision bounded by current Authority for the exact action, target, purpose, constraints, and time.

title: Use risk-appropriate authentication
requirement: Authentication strength, freshness, liveness, device evidence, and step-up requirements MUST be proportionate to the protected consequence and environmental risk.

title: Review access continuously
requirement: Privileged, cross-domain, sensitive-data, and protected-state access MUST be reviewed on grant, material change, periodic cadence, incident, role change, and termination.

title: Revoke promptly
requirement: Termination, compromise, expired delegation, quarantine, loss of need, or material risk increase MUST revoke or constrain affected sessions, tokens, permissions, and derived access without waiting for routine review.

title: Quarantine without identity erasure
requirement: Identity quarantine MUST restrict new work and credentials, preserve forensic evidence, maintain historical attribution, and require independent release; an identity MUST NOT self-release.

title: Prevent shared identities
requirement: Human operators MUST NOT share identities; service identities MUST be uniquely attributable to one workload identity and accountable owner.

title: Minimize access
requirement: Permissions MUST be purpose-bound, least-privileged, scoped to resources and operations, and expire at the shortest practicable interval consistent with declared availability, integrity, and human-harm constraints.

title: Broker privileged access
requirement: Privileged access MUST use an approved broker or equivalent controlled path with strong authentication, current Authority and Permission, session bounds, command or action evidence, and automatic expiry.

title: Use just-in-time elevation
requirement: Standing privilege SHOULD NOT exist; elevation MUST be just-in-time, purpose-specific, time-limited, approved at the appropriate risk level, and removed automatically.

title: Constrain break-glass
requirement: Break-glass access MUST require a declared emergency, narrow scope, an independent Permission decision bounded by current Authority where reachable, enhanced monitoring, immutable evidence, automatic expiry, and retrospective review within 24 hours.

title: Protect Owner ceremonies
requirement: Credentials or privileged access MUST NOT substitute for the Owner Authorization Ceremony or other constitutionally protected approval.

title: Issue workload-bound service identities
requirement: Each service identity MUST bind to an approved workload, environment, owner, capability need, permitted audience, credential method, and rotation/revocation policy.

title: Eliminate embedded credentials
requirement: Credentials MUST NOT be stored in source, images, logs, tickets, prompts, generated artifacts, or unapproved configuration; discovery MUST trigger containment and rotation.

title: Rotate on defined triggers
requirement: Credentials MUST rotate on scheduled lifetime, exposure, custody change, algorithm or issuer weakness, workload change, environment migration, and incident direction.

title: Investigate privileged anomalies
requirement: Unexpected privilege use, failed elevation, geographic or workload mismatch, bulk access, disabled telemetry, or policy bypass attempt MUST create an incident-relevant event and risk-based response.

title: Use approved cryptographic profiles
requirement: Cryptography MUST use approved algorithms, modes, key sizes, protocols, libraries, and purposes recorded in the cryptographic profile; custom cryptography is prohibited.

title: Separate keys by purpose and domain
requirement: Keys MUST be separated by environment, Trust Domain, principal or workload, purpose, data classification, and cryptographic operation; reuse across incompatible contexts is prohibited.

title: Keep secrets out of ambient authority
requirement: Secrets MUST be referenced through governed secret services, scoped to the least audience and capability, short-lived where practical, auditable, and incapable of independently granting Authority.

title: Protect key custody
requirement: High-impact keys MUST use hardware-backed or equivalently isolated custody, dual control for protected operations, non-exportability where feasible, and independently tested recovery.

title: Verify certificates completely
requirement: Certificate validation MUST verify chain, identity, purpose, constraints, time, revocation, algorithm policy, and expected Trust Domain; possession alone MUST NOT imply Authority or Permission.

title: Rotate and revoke safely
requirement: Rotation and revocation MUST define overlap, propagation, caches, in-flight work, offline nodes, failure behavior, receipts, and completion checks without weakening authority enforcement.

title: Plan cryptographic agility
requirement: Every cryptographic dependency MUST identify replacement triggers, compatible migration path, inventory reachability, testing, rollback or forward recovery, and retained evidence.

title: Respond to cryptographic compromise
requirement: Suspected key or issuer compromise MUST trigger containment, revocation, dependency impact analysis, reissuance, evidence preservation, and Book VIII-scoped reverification before restored trust.

title: Harden from declared baselines
requirement: Hosts, runtimes, containers, orchestrators, and managed services MUST conform to versioned hardening baselines with deviations recorded, time-bounded, monitored, and tested.

title: Segment by trust and authority
requirement: Network and workload paths MUST be allow-listed by authenticated identity, declared need, Trust Domain, data class, and permitted operation; network location MUST NOT establish trust.

title: Isolate workloads
requirement: Workloads MUST have separate identities, least resources, restricted host access, read-only roots where practical, controlled egress, bounded persistence, and containment against neighboring compromise.

title: Build reproducibly
requirement: Release artifacts MUST be produced by isolated, pinned, reviewable builds with protected inputs, deterministic steps where feasible, independent verification, and no developer workstation as release authority.

title: Sign and verify provenance
requirement: Artifacts, dependencies, policies, configurations, and critical data packages MUST carry verifiable provenance and integrity; failed or unknown provenance MUST block protected use.

title: Maintain dependency inventories
requirement: Every deployable unit MUST have a current transitive inventory, ownership, source, version, license disposition, integrity, support status, known risk, and replacement path.

title: Assume component compromise
requirement: Architecture and operations MUST constrain a compromised node, provider, dependency, model, adapter, or service from acquiring authority, mutating foreign authoritative state, suppressing audit, or escaping its domain.

title: Control external build services
requirement: External builders, registries, repositories, and vendors MUST be separate Trust Domains with explicit permitted exchanges, evidence, revocation paths, and no implicit constitutional trust.

title: Maintain exposure-aware inventory
requirement: The vulnerability program MUST continuously map assets, versions, dependencies, internet and cross-domain exposure, identities, privileges, data classes, and authoritative responsibilities.

title: Accept findings from multiple channels
requirement: Automated scans, advisories, dependency intelligence, researcher reports, penetration tests, incidents, anomaly evidence, and internal review MUST enter one tracked disposition process.

title: Prioritize by HAL consequence
requirement: Remediation priority MUST consider exploitability, exposure, privilege, authority path, data sensitivity, trust boundary, component ownership, containment, detectability, recovery, and credible harm—not severity score alone.

title: Meet risk-based remediation targets
requirement: Critical exploitable findings affecting authority, constitutional controls, protected state, external trust, or sensitive data MUST receive immediate containment and an approved remediation deadline.

title: Test patches before adoption
requirement: Patches MUST undergo impact analysis, provenance validation, representative testing, rollback or forward-recovery preparation, and post-update verification proportional to urgency and consequence.

title: Do not remove critical checks for urgency
requirement: Emergency remediation MAY compress ordinary timing but MUST NOT bypass identity, Authority, constitutional invariants, provenance, evidence, or recovery controls.

title: Verify closure
requirement: A finding closes only when the fix or compensating control is deployed to every in-scope asset, independently verified, monitored, and linked to residual risk; ticket closure alone is insufficient.

title: Coordinate disclosure safely
requirement: Disclosure MUST protect affected people, preserve evidence, respect authorized reporting channels and Treaties, avoid enabling preventable harm, and never conceal material risk from accountable decision-makers.
exception_authority: Owner only for genuine Owner matters

title: Classify before processing
requirement: Data MUST be classified before collection, inference, storage, use, disclosure, replication, or deletion; unknown classification MUST receive the most protective plausible handling.

title: Prove purpose and authority
requirement: Every personal or sensitive-data operation MUST bind an authorized purpose, applicable Authority or consent basis, permitted processing, recipients, retention, and evidence.

title: Collect the minimum
requirement: Collection MUST be limited to fields, precision, frequency, population, duration, and sources demonstrably necessary for the authorized purpose; convenience and possible future use are insufficient.

title: Prevent incompatible reuse
requirement: Data MUST NOT be reused, combined, enriched, modeled, or disclosed for a materially different purpose without a new valid authority and privacy assessment.

title: Set enforceable retention
requirement: Every data class MUST have an accountable retention rule, trigger, duration, legal or constitutional holds, archive behavior, backup treatment, and verifiable disposal path.

title: Honor deletion across derived stores
requirement: Authorized deletion MUST address authoritative records, replicas, caches, indexes, embeddings, models where technically applicable, exports, and backups, while preserving required constitutional and incident accountability.

title: Provide confidentiality- and integrity-protected access and export
requirement: Access or export MUST verify requester identity and Authority, obtain Permission for the exact subject and purpose, preserve provenance and context, use authenticated, confidentiality- and integrity-protected delivery, and prevent disclosure of others' rights or secrets.

title: Minimize privacy evidence
requirement: Privacy compliance evidence MUST prove the decision without unnecessarily reproducing sensitive content; access to evidence MUST itself be classified, authorized, logged, and reviewed.

title: Assess inference risk
requirement: Systems that infer identity, traits, relationships, emotion, health, beliefs, vulnerability, location, or intent MUST document necessity, uncertainty, affected people, misuse paths, validation, disclosure, retention, and denial or appeal.

title: Do not promote inference to fact
requirement: Inferred personal information MUST remain labeled with provenance, method, confidence, time, and contradiction; it MUST NOT be represented as observed fact or used beyond authorized purpose.

title: Prohibit covert expansion
requirement: HAL MUST NOT increase observation, persistence, profiling, audience, or disclosure merely because a capability makes it possible; material expansion requires explicit authority and review.

title: Preserve human dignity and agency
requirement: Interfaces MUST make consequential collection, inference, disclosure, recording, and automated effects understandable and provide meaningful consent, correction, refusal, or escalation where constitutionally applicable.
exception_authority: Owner only for genuine value conflict

title: Test privacy failure paths
requirement: Privacy tests MUST cover wrong subject, overcollection, purpose drift, unauthorized audience, inference leakage, retention expiry, incomplete deletion, backup restore, cross-domain transfer, and evidence overexposure.

title: Detect privacy incidents
requirement: Unauthorized, excessive, inaccurate, misleading, purpose-incompatible, retained-too-long, or improperly disclosed processing MUST enter the incident process even when no conventional security breach occurred.

title: Contain without destroying accountability
requirement: Privacy incident containment MUST stop further harm, restrict access and exchange, preserve minimized evidence, identify affected data and people, and avoid deleting records needed for accountable investigation.

title: Remediate affected lifecycle paths
requirement: Privacy remediation MUST address authoritative and derived stores, models, caches, backups, recipients, Treaties, purpose rules, access paths, and recurrence controls, with Book VIII reverification where claims were affected.

title: Classify every Trust Domain
requirement: Every internal or external domain MUST have stable identity, owner, boundary, permitted purposes, data and capability scope, security and privacy assumptions, evidence, review cadence, and failure behavior.

title: Keep trust distinct
requirement: Trust Assessment MAY inform decisions but MUST NOT create Identity, Permission, Authority, capability, Treaty scope, or authoritative state; current Permission remains independently required.
evidence: Trust Assessment and Permission Decision Record

title: Route cross-domain exchange through the Firewall
requirement: Every cross-domain ingress and egress MUST traverse the Constitutional Firewall with authenticated domain identity, active applicable Treaty where required, current Authority, purpose, classification, minimization, provenance, and integrity checks.

title: Fail closed on missing boundary facts
requirement: Absent, stale, ambiguous, unverifiable, expired, revoked, suspended, drifted, or incompatible domain, Treaty, Authority, schema, provenance, or integrity evidence MUST deny or quarantine the exchange.

title: Constrain returned data and effects
requirement: Firewall egress and ingress MUST enforce permitted direction, purpose, fields, classification, volume, frequency, recipients, actions, retention, and downstream propagation.

title: Preserve cross-domain provenance
requirement: Accepted exchanges MUST retain source domain, identities, Treaty and Authority context, schema and contract versions, integrity, time confidence, transformations, and custody.

title: Monitor domain drift
requirement: Control, ownership, identity, endpoint, jurisdiction, purpose, behavior, assurance, incident, or threat changes MUST trigger Trust Assessment and Treaty applicability review.

title: Exercise boundary failure
requirement: The program MUST test replay, substitution, downgrade, schema confusion, revoked Treaty, stale Authority, over-purpose, over-data, exfiltration, unavailable Firewall, and compromised counterparty scenarios.

title: Perform Treaty due diligence
requirement: Before activation, the Treaty package MUST assess counterparty identity, ownership, purposes, data, capabilities, directions, controls, incidents, evidence, retention, deletion, jurisdiction, subcontractors, suspension, revocation, and exit.

title: Preserve Owner approval
requirement: No certification, security review, counterparty assurance, contract signature, credential, or technical connectivity MAY substitute for the constitutionally required Owner approval of a Treaty or new Treaty class.

title: Activate exact approved versions
requirement: Activation MUST bind the exact signed Treaty version, parties, domains, purposes, data classes, capabilities, directions, constraints, effective time, expiry, and Firewall policy; drift MUST block activation.
enforcement: Book IX contract and policy gate

title: Monitor Treaty obligations
requirement: Active Treaties MUST be monitored for expiry, permitted-use compliance, volume, recipients, incidents, assurance validity, retention, deletion, downstream sharing, and counterparty change.

title: Suspend on material uncertainty
requirement: Material incident, assurance loss, identity doubt, policy drift, contract mismatch, noncompliance, or revocation unreachability MUST suspend affected exchange pending review.

title: Revoke comprehensively
requirement: Revocation MUST stop new exchange, handle in-flight actions, invalidate cached permissions, quarantine affected data, notify authorized parties, preserve evidence, and evaluate dependent capabilities and certifications.

title: Control subcontractors and fourth parties
requirement: A third party MUST NOT extend access, data, capability, or processing to another domain unless the Treaty explicitly permits it and equivalent identity, security, privacy, evidence, and revocation controls are verified.

title: Exit safely
requirement: Treaty expiry or termination MUST define return or deletion, retained evidence, credential and endpoint revocation, data quarantine, unresolved transactions, continuity, disputes, and post-exit verification.

title: Emit incident-relevant events
requirement: Identity, Authority, policy, privilege, secret, key, build, vulnerability, Firewall, Treaty, data, configuration, integrity, evidence, and recovery controls MUST emit structured success, denial, anomaly, and failure events.

title: Use canonical telemetry context
requirement: Events MUST carry the applicable Book IX identity, correlation, causation, time, provenance, classification, integrity, contract/schema version, and optional Authority and Treaty context; missing critical context MUST reduce trust.

title: Minimize and protect telemetry
requirement: Telemetry MUST exclude secrets and unnecessary sensitive content, apply field protection and access controls, use declared retention, and preserve sufficient evidence to reconstruct protected actions.

title: Detect authority violations separately
requirement: Detection content MUST identify attempted or actual excess Authority, stale delegation, bypassed Kernel or Firewall, foreign state mutation, and unauthorized Reality Boundary effects separately from compromise indicators.

title: Validate detection quality
requirement: Critical detections MUST have test cases, required sources, expected latency, false-negative and false-positive review, owner, runbook, evidence links, and behavior for missing telemetry.

title: Triage by consequence
requirement: Triage MUST assess constitutional impact, Authority, protected state, privacy, Trust Domain, Treaty, blast radius, persistence, evidence integrity, and recovery—not just technical severity.

title: Protect evidence pipelines
requirement: Critical event collection MUST be tamper-evident, access-controlled, time-aware, resilient, independently monitored, and incapable of being silently disabled by the observed component.

title: Measure coverage honestly
requirement: Coverage metrics MUST identify unmonitored assets, stale rules, missing fields, collection gaps, delayed events, untested scenarios, and blind spots; aggregate alert volume MUST NOT serve as assurance.

title: Declare incidents by consequence
requirement: Events MUST be declared incidents when credible impact involves constitutional invariants, Authority, identity, protected state, sensitive data, Trust Domains, Treaties, evidence, or continuity, even if technical certainty is incomplete.

title: Establish one incident command
requirement: Each incident MUST have one accountable Incident Commander, scope, objectives, decision log, roles, communication channels, evidence custodian, status cadence, and transfer procedure.

title: Contain proportionately
requirement: Containment MUST prioritize human safety, constitutional invariants, Owner access, Authority restriction, privacy, evidence, and blast-radius reduction; it MUST document intended and collateral effects.

title: Preserve chain of custody
requirement: Investigation evidence MUST record identity, source, time and confidence, collection method, digest, classification, custody, access, transformations, analysis, and disposition; originals MUST be preserved where feasible.

title: Separate facts from hypotheses
requirement: Investigations MUST distinguish observed facts, reported claims, analytical hypotheses, confidence, contradictions, unknowns, and decisions; later findings MUST supersede rather than rewrite history.

title: Coordinate privacy and trust response
requirement: Incidents involving personal data or external domains MUST engage Privacy and Trust Stewards, enforce Treaty duties, minimize shared evidence, and coordinate suspension, notification, and remediation.

title: Notify with verified scope
requirement: Notifications MUST be timely, authorized, accurate about known and unknown facts, purpose-limited, privacy-minimized, updateable, and linked to applicable Treaty, legal, operational, and governance duties.

title: Prevent incident authority expansion
requirement: Emergency status MUST NOT grant undeclared strategic authority, alter constitutional invariants, create Treaties or capabilities, or permit unrestricted access; emergency powers MUST be explicit and expire.

title: Recover from independently verified foundations
requirement: Compromise recovery MUST re-establish measured hardware or host integrity, immutable identity, current Authority, protected configuration, verified artifacts, evidence integrity, and authoritative state before restoring capability.

title: Scope eradication to dependencies
requirement: Eradication MUST address persistence, credentials, keys, images, builds, dependencies, policies, data, peers, Treaties, caches, backups, and compromised evidence—not only the initially affected host.

title: Require post-recovery verification
requirement: Restored systems MUST complete risk-based Book VIII verification, including containment, authority paths, privacy, trust boundaries, recovery invariants, and regression, before protected work resumes.

title: Authorize offensive testing
requirement: Penetration tests and red teams MUST have written scope, targets, time, allowed techniques, data handling, safety boundaries, stop authority, escalation, evidence, and cleanup before execution.

title: Test both attacker and overreach paths
requirement: Adversarial work MUST test compromise of HAL and misuse or excess of HAL Authority, including stale delegation, trust confusion, Treaty bypass, evidence suppression, and unauthorized external effect.

title: Remediate findings with independent closure
requirement: Offensive and audit findings MUST enter the common risk process and close only after deployed remediation, independent retest, residual-risk decision, and affected-assurance review.

title: Prepare auditable evidence
requirement: Audit packages MUST state scope, criteria, sources, sampling, limitations, control owners, evidence locations, access decisions, exceptions, findings, remediation, and unresolved risk without fabricating assurance.

title: Supply but do not issue certification
requirement: Book VI MUST supply security, privacy, trust, incident, recovery, and control-effectiveness evidence to Book VIII; Book VI roles MUST NOT issue or redefine certification unless separately authorized there.

title: Measure outcomes and control health
requirement: Metrics MUST cover prevention, detection, containment, recovery, authority denials, privacy outcomes, trust-boundary enforcement, evidence quality, exceptions, remediation, and recurrence.

title: Prevent vanity metrics
requirement: Alert count, patch count, scan count, training completion, coverage percentage, or audit completion MUST NOT alone demonstrate effective risk reduction or constitutional conformance.

title: Track leading and lagging signals
requirement: Each critical risk MUST have outcome, control-effectiveness, exposure, evidence-freshness, and failure signals with owners, thresholds, cadence, and response.

title: Learn without rewriting history
requirement: Improvements MUST preserve prior incidents, findings, decisions, exceptions, evidence, and dissent; updated understanding MUST be versioned and linked to outcomes.

title: Reconcile Book IX contracts
requirement: Security events, Authority context, Treaty exchange, Firewall decisions, errors, schemas, and protocol behaviors MUST map to final Book IX identifiers and MUST NOT invent alternate wire contracts.

title: Reconcile Book VIII assurance
requirement: Control tests, incidents, penetration results, privacy assessments, Treaty evidence, recovery, and continuous signals MUST map into Book VIII claims, evidence, certification status, and recertification triggers.

title: Review the program periodically
requirement: At least annually and after material incidents or canon changes, an independent review MUST assess source fidelity, control effectiveness, gaps, burden, exceptions, evidence, roles, metrics, and needed revisions.

title: Certify Book VI conformance honestly
requirement: Book VI conformance MAY be declared only when mandatory controls are mapped, applicable evidence is current, critical failures are resolved or operation is constrained, reconciliations are current, and no contradiction remains.
